name: English Opening
description: A flexible flank-opening course that teaches positional play, center control from the side, and calm development.

branches.title: Main Line: c4 and Nc3
branches.description: Learn the default English setup: control d5 from the side and develop flexibly.

moves.title: Control d5
moves.explanation: c4 fights for d5 from the side and keeps the center flexible. c4 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The English controls the center from the side, then develops quietly before choosing a central break.

moves.title: Black takes space
moves.explanation: Black occupies the center directly. e5 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The English controls the center from the side, then develops quietly before choosing a central break.

moves.title: Develop toward d5
moves.explanation: Nc3 develops and increases control over d5. White can choose the center structure later. Nc3 develops a knight to c3. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Develop to f6
moves.explanation: Nf6 develops a knight to f6. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Improve with g3
moves.explanation: g3 is a practical improving move for White. In real games, keep asking: is my king safe, are my pieces active, and what central pawn break comes next?

moves.title: Get the king safe
moves.explanation: O-O moves the king to safety and brings the rook closer to the center. This is usually the moment when the opening becomes an early middlegame plan: The English controls the center from the side, then develops quietly before choosing a central break.

moves.title: Get the king safe
moves.explanation: O-O gets the king safe and brings a rook closer to the center. This is the bridge from opening to middlegame: now look for your worst piece, your safest trade, and your best pawn break.

moves.title: Develop to e6
moves.explanation: Be6 improves a piece and adds control over important squares. Developed pieces create threats naturally, so you do not need to force an attack before castling.

After each move, check king safety, center control, and piece activity.
When a trade appears, ask what file opens and which piece improves next.

ideas: Stay flexible before committing central pawns.
Develop naturally and avoid rushing attacks.
The English controls the center from the side, then develops quietly before choosing a central break.
Trade only when it improves your position, removes danger, or opens a useful file.
By move 8-12, you should know your early middlegame plan: safe king, active pieces, and one central break.
commonMistakes: Treating c4 like a gambit trick.
Ignoring development because the center is quiet.
Pushing too many pawns before pieces are out.
Stopping after memorized moves and playing without a plan.
Trading automatically without asking what improves afterward.
Starting an attack before castling or finishing development.
